lines.text: Ridehail is a ride-sharing platform: customers, drivers and operations, working together in real time.
A customer signs up in the customer app, while a driver signs up in the rider app.
The driver goes online and shares their position. The customer adds a payment card; in this demo, a test card.
The customer searches for a destination by name. The map shows the real road to it, and the fare is quoted upfront, with demand-based pricing.
The request goes to the nearest driver, who sees it in real time with the road on a map, and accepts.
Now the customer watches the car approach on the live map, with its position updated every few seconds.
The driver arrives, starts the trip, and the car follows the road to the destination.
When the trip ends, the card is charged automatically, and the driver's earnings are credited through a double-entry ledger.
Now the busy case: three customers request a ride at the very same moment.
The nearest driver sees all three requests at once, each on its own map, and takes one. The others go to drivers nearby.
On the operations map, every request and every driver is visible live.
Operations see what needs attention, every payment, and a ledger that must always balance.
Chargebacks are tracked and answered from here, and every administrator action is written to an audit log.
Built and tested end to end: a Spring Boot API, web and phone apps, and Stripe payments and payouts.
